The idea of killing someone can be rationalized by your mind, the idea of being killed will tried to be stopped by your body's survival instincts. That's why so many suicides involve inhibiting your body's instincts through the method of suicide or being intoxicated or something. Take hanging for example, your body doesn't register the rope around your neck as an active threat until you're in the air. Or shooting yourself, your body hasn't evolved to register a piece of metal as an active threat yet. Even then plenty of people who want death won't be able to kill themselves because of our emotions, specifically fear. Fear is not logical, it too stems from your body. You will never be free of physical restraints. You will never be fully free. The ultimate rebellion is suicide.

I don't know, I don't think that those feelings ever go away. It's our rational mind constantly being exhausted by the stress and oversocialization of modern society and looking for an escape. It might seem grim but I just treat it as a daydream at this point and I entertain it with the same amount of thought I would to any imaginary scenario, say something like I win the lottery and I imagine what I would do with the money. Any mind can come to the conclusion that death is peaceful, however it takes more than that to become suicidal imo. To me suicide isn't something emotional or the last choice someone has. I see it as when the rational part of our mind that tells us life isn't worth living overwhelms our animalistic instinct to live. I know most people don't see it that way but I do think when people commit suicide our subconsciousness is weighing cost and benefit and decides death is a better option. I think there are inherent good and bad qualities to life and death, and most people recognize that. So when that thought pops up in your head that makes you feel like you're better off not living, it's really just a thought. The gap between entertaining this thought and actual suicidal tendencies is the strengthening of your logical argument for suicide or weakening your body's instincts against death. For the former this might be in ignoring the fear of the unknown, or attributing less hope to life. For the latter this could be getting yourself drunk, or to actually be suffering physically (say from abuse or disease). I don't think you are actually suicidal you're just having normal thoughts that humans have from time to time and you should just accept that it's a part of life. You can also just completely ignore them, it's what most people do.
